# Checkmate Dynamics: full site text

> Motor, sensing and sync nodes on one USB-C bus, from a robotics hardware company in Dallas, Texas. Makers use them one at a time, robotics companies build them in, and our data-station hardware is assembled from them. Prices are list prices in US dollars.

Specifications are design values until a unit is measured; “Target” and “Est.” mark goals and estimates. Prices are list prices in USD. Images are concept renders. Every page has a markdown version at the same address ending in .md.

---

**03** System

## One cable per device.

Each node’s own USB-C port is the bus: power negotiated over PD, USB to a computer, and CAN to everything else. On a bench, a phone charger runs one node. On a floor, a Hub 8 Pro runs eight.

|  |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | SmartStepper 17 |  | USB-C, PD + USB + CAN 1 Mbit/s |  |
| A2 | SmartServo G × n |  | USB-C, CAN-FD |  |
| B1 | Contour |  | USB-C, depth and sync in |  |
| C1 | Sync Beacon |  | USB-C, station clock |  |
| D1 | Hub 8 Pro |  | 8 node ports with PD per port, 2 accessory ports, CAN star with isolated ports, 20 V motor rail, E-stop in |  |
| PC | Host PC |  | One USB device. Python SDK, ROS 2, LeRobot, MCAP |  |

Fig. 02 — Bus topology. Hub 8 Pro ports are point-to-point segments, so a damaged cable is cut off without stopping the others.

**04** Test card

## Every unit ships with its own numbers.

Each node is calibrated and measured at final test, and the results go in the box and stay on the node. We publish measured values. Anything we haven’t measured yet is marked as a target.

- Encoder calibration stored on the node, not in a laptop’s config file
- Backlash, backdrive and torque recorded per serial number
- The same record goes to makers, OEM customers and our own stations

**Unit test card** SmartServo G-2804 · 20:1

Illustrative

Serial | CM-A23-000127

Encoder calibration | 16,384 counts/turn | at test

Backlash, output | 4.6 arcmin | at test

Backdrive, unpowered | 0.21 N·m | at test

Continuous torque, 20 V | 0.93 N·m | at test

Thermal soak, 30 min | 41 °C | at test

PD contract | 20 V | at test

Illustrative values. Each unit’s real values are measured at final test. | Dallas, TX

# One family of nodes.

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/products.html

Products | Four families · one bus

Every product is a finished unit that works on its own and joins the same USB-C bus as the rest. Learn one and you know the next: same cable, same status light, same app.

**A** Move

## Motor nodes with everything inside.

Driver, encoder, controller and gearbox built in and calibrated as one unit. Reducers are part of the nodes, not separate parts.

**A1** SmartStepper 17 From $79

Closed-loop NEMA 17. Board, direct-drive node, or with a 25:1 metal cycloidal.

**A2** SmartServo G From $89

Brushless servo for 2804 and 5208 gimbal motors, direct drive or cycloidal. The Leader’s joints.

**B** Sense

## The scene around the robot, the angle inside the joint.

Contour | **54 × 42 zones**

Wireframe from CAD

**B1–B2** Contour, Contour Wrist Waitlist

Metric time-of-flight depth over USB-C, synced to your cameras. The Wrist version rides on the gripper.

**B3** Output encoder $29

Reads a reducer’s output angle directly. Standard on geared nodes, sold for retrofit.

**C** Sync

## An instrument for the station.

The Sync Beacon doesn’t measure the scene or a joint. It is a clock your cameras film, so every stream can be placed on one timeline and checked against the others. That’s why it has a family of its own.

[Sync Beacon](https://checkmatedynamics.com/sync-beacon.html)

A 14-day timing check is $1,250 per station; owning a beacon is $999. Patent pending.

**Station Report** episode 000127

Gold

Cross-camera skew | 0.21 ms | Gold

Frame drops | 0 / 1,812 | Gold

Drift, session | 0.40 ms/h | Pass

Illustrative values | C1

**D** Power & connect

## One cable per device.

**D1** Hub 8 Pro $399

Eight node ports, per-port power and CAN, hardware e-stop.

**D2** Bus cable In the box

Power, USB and CAN on one USB-C cable. An anodized Cable Clip holds it in the port; one comes with every node.

**D3** I/O tile $19

Qwiic and AUX ports for SmartServo G.

# SmartStepper 17

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/smartstepper-17.html

[Products](https://checkmatedynamics.com/products.html) / A — Move / A1 | Closed-loop stepper node

A closed-loop NEMA 17 that runs on a USB-C charger and sets up in a browser. Add the 25:1 metal cycloidal and it becomes a robot joint.

**A1.1 · Board** | Controller for your own NEMA 17 | **$79**

**A1.2 · SmartStepper 17 · Direct** | Direct drive: board on a calibrated NEMA 17, housed | **$169**

**A1.3 · SmartStepper 17 · 25:1** | Cycloidal reducer and output encoder | **$279**

[Register interest](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Register%20interest%3A%20SmartStepper%2017) | [Volume / OEM](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Parts%20and%20OEM%20enquiry%3A%20SmartStepper%2017)

This device has not been authorized as required by the rules of the Federal Communications Commission. This device is not, and may not be, offered for sale or lease, or sold or leased, until authorization is obtained.

*Output flange · M3 bolt circle, dowels* *25:1 cycloidal · 42 mm square* *NEMA 17 · flying-lead or socketed* *Rear unit · controller, 45.3 mm square* *USB-C · PD, USB, CAN*

**Fig. 01** SmartStepper 17 · 25:1, three-quarter view Concept render

Key figures

- **Encoder**: 14-bit, 16,384 counts
- **Power**: USB-C PD, 5–20 V
- **Bus**: CAN 1 Mbit/s
- **Reduction**: 25:1 cycloidal
- **Backlash**: ~7 arcmin Est.
- **Gearbox**: 42 mm square

45.3 mm

42 mm

Plan view, to scale | Diagram

**01** Overview

## A stepper that knows where it is.

01

### Closed loop

A 14-bit magnetic encoder (16,384 counts per turn) watches the shaft, so a stall is reported instead of silently losing position.

02

### USB-C power

Any USB-C Power Delivery charger supplies 5 to 20 V. The same port carries USB to a laptop and CAN to the next node.

03

### Browser setup

The Checkmate app runs in your browser: calibrate, set current, jog, and plot angle, current and temperature live.

04

### Your NEMA 17 or ours

Works with flying-lead or socketed NEMA 17 motors (adapter included). The leads plug into the rear unit; closed loop needs a rear shaft for the encoder magnet.

**02** Direct drive

## The motor shaft is the output.

SmartStepper 17 · Direct is the complete node with no reducer: the same closed-loop board and calibrated NEMA 17, housed, with the shaft driving your load.

01

### Full motor speed

No gearbox between the motor and the load. For turntables, slides, fixtures and printer or CNC axes that need speed more than torque.

02

### Nothing to wear

No reducer means no backlash from gearing and no gear stage to service. The encoder watches the shaft that does the work.

03

### Geared later

The 25:1 reducer bolts to the motor face. A direct node becomes A1.3 for the price difference, and keeps its identity and calibration history.

List price $169. Direct-drive output covers and frames are in design.

**03** Reducer

## A metal cycloidal inside the motor’s own footprint.

Two cycloid discs share the load across many rollers, which keeps the joint stiff and low in backlash without growing past the 42 mm outline.

- Lost motion about 7 arcmin (estimate), measured per unit
- Torque targets 4 N·m continuous, 8.5 N·m peak
- Output encoder fitted as standard
- Output face with M3 bolt circle and dowel holes

*Output carrier* *Cycloid discs × 2* *Motor body, exposed*

**Fig. 02** Quarter section of the reducer Concept render

**04** Integration

*Controller board* *NEMA 17 · flying leads*

**Fig. 03** Rear unit: magnet, frame, board, cover Concept render

## Drops into a printer, a CNC or an arm.

Drive it over CAN from Python, or take STEP/DIR from Klipper, Marlin or GRBL boards on the AUX port. To Klipper it is an ordinary external driver.

- Qwiic port for I²C sensors and displays
- AUX: STEP/DIR, endstop, UART or sync
- Chain nodes over CAN on the same cable
- An anodized aluminum Cable Clip holds the USB-C cable in place (in the box)

**05** Specification

|  | SmartStepper 17 · Direct | SmartStepper 17 · 25:1 |
|---|---|---|
| Motor | NEMA 17, pre-mounted and calibrated. Board: your own flying-lead or socketed NEMA 17 (adapter included) with a rear shaft for the encoder magnet | Same, with 25:1 metal cycloidal |
| Size | 45.3 mm square rear unit | 42 mm square gearbox · 45.3 mm square rear unit |
| Controller / driver | ESP32-S3 (USB; Wi-Fi and BLE off by default, enabled in the app) / TMC2209 | Same |
| Encoder | MT6701, 14-bit, motor shaft | Same, plus output encoder |
| Power | USB-C PD sink, 5–20 V | Same |
| Bus | CAN 1 Mbit/s on the USB-C cable | Same |
| Ports | USB-C · Qwiic · AUX 4-pin JST-SH | Same |
| Backlash | — | ~7 arcmin Estimate |
| Torque | Motor-dependent, measured per unit | 4 N·m cont. / 8.5 N·m peak Target |
| Software | Checkmate browser app · Python SDK · Klipper STEP/DIR guide |  |
| Compliance | FCC Part 15B testing before shipping · US only at launch |  |

CAN needs a full-featured USB-C cable; charge-only cables don’t carry it. Targets are design goals; every unit ships with its measured test card.

**06** Figures

## The node from other angles.

**Fig. 05** Rear unit, Cable Clip on USB-C

# SmartServo G

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/smartservo-g.html

[Products](https://checkmatedynamics.com/products.html) / A — Move / A2 | Brushless gimbal-motor servo

A complete brushless actuator: gimbal motor, field-oriented control, magnetic encoder and housing, on one USB-C cable. The Checkmate Leader is built from these.

**A2.1 · Board** | One board for 2804 and 5208 motors | **$89**

**A2.2 · G-2804 · Direct** | Direct drive, no gearbox, no backlash | **$159**

**A2.3 · G-2804 · 20:1** | Cycloidal, output encoder, I/O tile | **$249**

**A2.4 · G-5208 · Direct** | Direct drive, larger motor | **$249**

**A2.5 · G-5208 · 25:1** | Cycloidal, output encoder, I/O tile | **$399**

[Register interest](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Register%20interest%3A%20SmartServo%20G) | [Volume / OEM](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Parts%20and%20OEM%20enquiry%3A%20SmartServo%20G)

This device has not been authorized as required by the rules of the Federal Communications Commission. This device is not, and may not be, offered for sale or lease, or sold or leased, until authorization is obtained.

*G-2804 · iFlight GBM2804H-100T* *G-5208 · iFlight GM5208, 24 winding*

**Fig. 01** SmartServo G nodes, both motor sizes Concept render

Key figures

- **Motors**: 2804 · 5208
- **Reduction**: 20:1 · 25:1
- **Encoder**: 14-bit
- **Power**: USB-C PD, 5–20 V
- **Bus**: CAN-FD
- **Torque**: Per unit Test card

Ø35 mm

Controller board, to scale | Diagram

**01** Overview

## Built for feel and fidelity, not raw force.

01

### Quiet

Field-oriented control on a gimbal motor: smooth motion with no stepping and almost no sound.

02

### Absolute

A 14-bit encoder on the motor axis with calibration stored on the node. Geared versions add an output encoder.

03

### Backdrivable

Move it by hand and record the motion. Made for leader arms, wrists, grippers, camera heads and haptics.

04

### One cable

USB-C PD power and CAN-FD between nodes on the same cable. Setup runs in the Checkmate app in your browser.

Not for lifting shoulders or wheels. For those you want a higher-torque actuator, and we’ll say so.

**02** Direct drive

## No gearbox between you and the motor.

G-2804 · Direct and G-5208 · Direct are complete nodes with the gimbal motor driving your load. Both use the same board, the same cable and the same app as the geared nodes.

01

### Backdrivable

With no gear stage to fight, the shaft can be moved by hand. That is the feel haptics, knobs and hand-held controls depend on.

02

### Smooth and quiet

Field-oriented control on a gimbal motor, with no gear stage to add backlash.

03

### Test fixtures and benches

Rate tables, load stages, camera heads and teaching benches need speed and clean torque more than reduction. The G-5208 · Direct is the larger of the two.

List prices $159 and $249. Torque is measured per unit and printed on the test card. Direct-drive output covers and frames are in design.

**03** Construction

*I/O tile (optional)* *Ø35 mm controller board* *Base plate* *Gimbal motor*

**Fig. 02** The stack, 2804 version Concept render

## A round board that sits on the motor.

Controller, driver and encoder share one board on the motor’s back. The optional I/O tile stacks on top, and an aluminum cover closes it.

- STM32G431 controller, DRV8316 driver
- USB-C PD sink, capped at 20 V
- Calibration stored on the node
- Two dowels in every cap face for repeatable swaps

**04** Variants

## Two motors, direct or geared.

**A2.2–A2.3** G-2804 · Direct and G-2804 · 20:1 $159 / $249

Compact and light. Direct drive for handle roll, camera pan and haptic knobs. The 20:1 cycloidal for wrists, grippers and leader joints.

**A2.4–A2.5** G-5208 · Direct and G-5208 · 25:1 $249 / $399

Larger and stronger. Direct drive for haptics and camera heads. The 25:1 cycloidal for the heavier joints of a leader arm.

**05** Specification

|  | G-2804 · Direct | G-2804 · 20:1 | G-5208 · Direct | G-5208 · 25:1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Motor | iFlight GBM2804H-100T | iFlight GM5208, 24 winding |  |  |
| Reducer | Direct | 20:1 cycloidal | Direct | 25:1 cycloidal |
| Lost motion | 0 | ~8 arcmin Estimate | 0 | ~4 arcmin Estimate |
| Encoders | Motor, 14-bit | Motor + output | Motor, 14-bit | Motor + output |
| Torque | Measured per unit and printed on the test card; curves published after the first batch |  |  |  |
| Controller / driver | STM32G431 / DRV8316 |  |  |  |
| Power | USB-C PD sink, 5–20 V |  |  |  |
| Bus | CAN-FD on the USB-C cable; classic CAN when mixed with SmartStepper |  |  |  |
| I/O | Optional tile | Tile included | Optional tile | Tile included |
| Software | Checkmate browser app over USB (Chrome, Edge) · Python SDK · LeRobot |  |  |  |

Design values. Estimates and targets are marked; each unit ships with its own measured test card.

**06** Accessories

### D3 · I/O tile

Stacks on the board. Adds Qwiic and a 4-pin AUX port for sensors, endstops and triggers.

$19

Ring magnet and side sensor 3-axis

### B3 · Output encoder

A 3-axis magnetic sensor and ring magnet in the reducer cap. Standard on geared nodes, sold for retrofit.

$29

Full-featured USB-C carrying power, USB and CAN, with a clip that holds it in the port.

# Contour

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/contour.html

[Products](https://checkmatedynamics.com/products.html) / B — Sense / B1–B2 | Direct time-of-flight depth

Metric depth from a sensor the size of a thumb, over one USB-C cable and on the same clock as your cameras. It measures distance directly, so plain, textureless surfaces read as well as patterned ones.

**B1 · Contour** | USB-C depth sensor | **Register interest**

**B2 · Contour Wrist** | Gripper mount, on the station clock | **Stations**

**Contour OEM** | Module for your own housing | **Talk to us**

[Register interest](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Register%20interest%3A%20Contour) | [OEM enquiry](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Parts%20and%20OEM%20enquiry%3A%20Contour)

This device has not been authorized as required by the rules of the Federal Communications Commission. This device is not, and may not be, offered for sale or lease, or sold or leased, until authorization is obtained.

Sensor figures from ST’s datasheet. Size and mass come from our design and will be replaced by measurements.

Resolution | **54 × 42 zones**

Field of view | **55° × 42°**

Frame rate | **30 Hz**

Sensor range | **0.05–8.8 m**

**Fig. 01** Contour development unit (case rev B), with the sensor’s figures Wireframe from CAD

Key figures

- **Sensor**: VL53L9CX
- **Wavelength**: 940 nm
- **Resolution**: 54 × 42
- **Frame rate**: 30 Hz
- **Mass**: 37 g Est.
- **Interface**: USB-C

45 mm

40 mm

Front view, to scale, est. | Diagram

**01** Overview

## Geometry at contact range.

01

### Metric

Direct time-of-flight returns absolute distance whatever the surface color or texture.

02

### Small

About 45 × 40 × 12 mm and under 40 g (target): light enough for a small follower arm’s gripper.

03

### On the clock

A sync input lines depth frames up with your RGB cameras and the rest of the station.

04

### In your pipeline

Appears as a camera in LeRobot, with depth and confidence for every frame.

**02** Contour Wrist

## Depth beside the gripper, next to the camera you already run.

Contour Wrist mounts on the follower’s wrist with adapters for common arms and adds contact-range depth on the station clock. It is in development alongside the [Sync Beacon](https://checkmatedynamics.com/sync-beacon.html).

- Station profile tuned for 5 cm to 1.5 m
- Per‑unit calibration file in the box
- Mounted on the follower, never the leader

Where it fits

| Lighting | Indoor, LED-lit stations |
|---|---|
| Frame rate | 30 Hz, depth + confidence |
| Resolution | 54 × 42 zones: contact geometry, not an RGB replacement |
| Not for | Direct sunlight, halogen lamps, scenes full of glass |

**03** Specification

| Sensor | ST VL53L9CX direct time-of-flight, 940 nm, Class 1 laser |
|---|---|
| Resolution | 54 × 42 zones; binned modes down to 4 × 4 |
| Field of view | 55° × 42° |
| Range | 0.05–8.8 m sensor range; 1.5 m clamp in the station profile |
| Frame rate | 30 Hz over USB, depth and confidence |
| Size, mass | About 45 × 40 × 12 mm, about 37 g Estimate |
| Power | USB-C; under 1 W in the station profile Target |
| Interfaces | USB-C · sync input |
| Software | LeRobot camera plugin · Python |

Sensor figures from ST’s datasheet. Size, mass and power come from our design and will be replaced by measurements.

# Hub 8 Pro

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/hub-8.html

[Products](https://checkmatedynamics.com/products.html) / D — Power & connect / D1 | Eight-port node hub

Powers, connects and protects a whole arm of nodes. Every port is its own USB-C power source and its own CAN segment, so one damaged cable can’t take the rest down.

**D1 · Hub 8 Pro** | Hub only; power supply optional | **$399**

[Talk to us](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Parts%20and%20OEM%20enquiry%3A%20Hub%208%20Pro) | [Book a call](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Data%20station%20call%3A%20Hub%208%20Pro)

Ships inside the Checkmate Leader and on its own.

This device has not been authorized as required by the rules of the Federal Communications Commission. This device is not, and may not be, offered for sale or lease, or sold or leased, until authorization is obtained.

*P1–P8 · node ports, PD + CAN each* *Machined 6061 case*

**Fig. 01** Hub 8 Pro, port side Concept render

Key figures

- **Node ports**: 8 + 2 accessory
- **Port power**: 20 V / 1.5 A Design
- **Bus**: CAN-FD star
- **Power in**: 12–48 V DC
- **Host**: 1 × USB
- **E-stop**: 2-channel NC

218 mm

120 mm

Plan view, to scale, est. | Diagram

**01** Overview

## A star, not a chain.

01

### Eight node ports

Plus two accessory ports for a Sync Beacon or Contour, and an upstream port to chain hubs for bimanual stations.

02

### Power per port

Each port is a USB-C PD source: off when empty, 20 V at 1.5 A once a node asks for it, and 3 A on up to two ports.

03

### Isolated CAN

Every port is its own CAN segment, bridged inside the hub. A crushed cable is cut off; the others keep running.

04

### Hardware e-stop

A two-channel input removes motor power in hardware, with no firmware in the path.

**02** Host

## One cable to the PC, one device for every node.

The hub appears as a single USB device whose CAN channels show up as standard SocketCAN interfaces on Linux. Each node’s own USB stays reachable for setup and updates.

- CAN-FD for SmartServo G, classic CAN for SmartStepper and accessories
- Shared 20 V motor rail: one node’s braking feeds another
- Per-port power and bus telemetry
- Machined aluminum case

*Power in* *E-stop · link · sync*

**Fig. 02** Rear panel Concept render

**03** Bus cable

**Fig. 03** A node’s USB-C cable held by the Cable Clip Concept render

## Power, USB and CAN on one cable.

Every Checkmate device uses its own USB-C port as the bus. Any full-featured USB-C cable carries all three; charge-only cables won’t carry CAN.

- One cable and one Cable Clip (anodized 6061) ship in every node box; extra clips $9
- The Clip Bar 8 screws across all eight ports and clamps every cable, so a snag can’t pull a joint offline

**04** Specification

| Ports | 8 node · 2 accessory · 1 upstream; USB-C with M2 threads for the Clip Bar 8 |
|---|---|
| Port power | USB-C PD source per port: 5 V on attach, 20 V / 1.5 A on request; 3 A on up to 2 ports |
| Bus | Active CAN star with CAN-FD and classic domains; ports isolated |
| Host link | One USB device per hub; SocketCAN-compatible channels |
| Safety | Two-channel normally-closed e-stop input; hardware cut of motor power |
| Power in | 12–48 V DC or USB-C PD; supply optional |
| Enclosure | Machined 6061 aluminum, about 218 × 120 × 34 mm Design |
| Cascading | Second hub’s upstream port into an accessory port; one hub per arm |

Design values for the current board. A unit has not been measured yet; each shipped unit comes with its own measured test card.

# Prove your cameras agree on time.

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/sync-beacon.html

[Stations](https://checkmatedynamics.com/stations.html) / C — Sync / C1 | Timing test instrument · Patent pending

Cameras, robot joints and sensors each keep their own clock. Your training data comes out misaligned, and most rigs never measure by how much. The Sync Beacon is a clock your cameras can film. It puts every frame on one timeline, and a Station Report shows the result.

**14-day rental** | A beacon ships to you, per station | **$1,250**

**Own one** | A founding Sync Beacon, yours | **$999**

[Book a timing check](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Sync%20Beacon%20timing%20check&body=Cameras%20and%20frame%20rates%3A%0ARobot%20and%20recorder%3A%0ALocation%3A) | See the offers

A timing test instrument for rig validation and QA. Sold to labs and companies.

**Fig. 01** Sync Beacon, exterior Wireframe from CAD

**01** The problem

## Every stream on your rig keeps its own time.

Each camera, joint log and depth stream stamps its data on a different clock. When they disagree, the dataset pairs images with the wrong joint readings.

01

### Cameras stamp late

A USB camera’s timestamp is usually when the host received the frame, not when the sensor exposed it. Buffers and USB scheduling put an unknown delay between the two.

02

### Clocks start apart and drift

Joint encoders log on the controller’s clock. Cameras log on the PC’s. They start at different moments and move apart over a session.

03

### Most rigs never measure it

Without a shared reference, skew shows up as a policy that almost works and an episode that gets rejected with no stated cause. Most rigs carry no number for it.

**—** Same moment

Beacon clock

Camera A

Camera B

Wrist camera

Joint log

**Fig. 02** One instant, four clocks. The dashed line marks the same moment Illustration

**frame_index / fps**

How LeRobot computes each recorded frame’s timestamp: from the frame counter, not from the camera. It records when the recorder counted the frame, not when the camera captured it.

[LeRobot source, dataset_writer.py line 225](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/626da71be9d21b3c740b6438514519a503a2d535/src/lerobot/datasets/dataset_writer.py#L225), read Oct 28, 2026

**02** The beacon

## A clock your cameras can film.

The beacon sits in view of your cameras and shows an LED clock that steps every 1 ms. Every camera films it. The decoder reads the clock in each frame, so every frame’s exposure time lands on one clock.

You get dropped frames, repeated frames, true frame intervals and the offset between cameras, per camera. It is built for any camera that can see it, and your Station Report confirms it on your cameras. Nothing is wired to the cameras, and nothing changes in your recorder.

**Fig. 03** The LED face: 8 × 8, stepping every 1 ms Illustration

**1 ms**

LED clock step. Selectable at 0.5 ms and 2 ms.

**8 × 8**

Green LED face, 525 nm. Green light passes the IR-cut filter on camera sensors.

**Any camera**

Built for webcams, machine-vision cameras and phones that can see the face. Your Station Report confirms each camera.

**03** Station Report

## Proof, not a feeling.

The Station Report lists, for each camera, how many frames were placed on the beacon clock, what was dropped or repeated, the true frame interval, and the offset to every other camera.

Keep it with the dataset. When a data buyer or a reviewer asks how well aligned the streams are, you have the measurement.

Accuracy on real cameras is measured for your rig in the Station Report.

**Station Report** session 03 · station B-04

Example

Camera A, frames on beacon clock | 1,799 / 1,800

Camera A, dropped · repeated | 1 · 0

Camera B, true frame interval | 33.4 ms

Camera B, offset to camera A | +6.2 ms

Wrist camera, offset to camera A | −11.8 ms

Shutter type · line time | rolling · 18 µs

Illustrative layout, example values. Not a measurement.

**04** How it works

## Place it, record a minute, read the report.

01

### Place it in view

Set the beacon where every camera can see its face, on a tripod or clamp. Up to 1.1 m from a 640 × 480 camera, 2.1 m at 720p, within 60° of straight on (calculated). Power by USB-C from your PC.

02

### Record a test session

Set a short manual exposure and lock focus on the face. Record every camera over the same 60 s.

03

### Decode and read

Run the decoder on each video on your PC. Every frame lands on the beacon clock, and the Station Report shows drops, repeats, intervals and camera-to-camera offset.

**05** Who it’s for

## Teams that need to know their rig is aligned.

Use it to check a rig before you record on it and again whenever the rig changes.

A

### Data-collection teams

Validate each new station before it records. Re-check after a camera swap, a USB change or a rebuild. Hand your buyer a measurement of the timing, not a promise.

B

### University labs

Know your cameras and arms line up before a study’s data collection starts, and put the figures in the methods. Invoiced by P-card, PO, card or ACH.

C

### Rig builders and integrators

Commission a station, find the camera that runs late and confirm the fix, with the same instrument on every rig you build.

**07** At a glance

## What it is, in numbers.

| LED clock | 1 ms step, with 0.5 ms and 2 ms selectable |
|---|---|
| LED face | 8 × 8 green LEDs, 525 nm |
| Cameras | Built for any camera that can see the face; confirmed per camera in the Station Report. No wiring to the camera |
| Placement | Up to 1.1 m from a 640 × 480 camera, 2.1 m at 720p, within 60° of straight on (calculated) |
| Reference pulses | Two SYNC outputs, 100 µs active-low pulses, 30 Hz by default |
| Clock stability | ±0.14 ppm over 3 h on the first unit measured (bench result, Oct 26, 2026). Each unit ships with its own calibration certificate |
| Power | USB-C, 5 V. No radio, no network |
| Mounting | 1/4”-20 tripod adapter |
| Decoder | Runs on your PC in Python 3 with numpy and OpenCV |

**01** Operator

## More good episodes per operator-hour.

01

### Weightless

Active gravity compensation at every joint. Operators guide the arm instead of holding it up.

02

### Felt limits

Haptic walls at the follower’s joint limits, and trigger force feedback from the follower’s gripper.

03

### No drift

Absolute encoders hold calibration through every power cycle. No re-zeroing at the start of a shift.

04

### Hands stay on

REC and DISCARD on the handle; the arm returns home between episodes on its own.

**02** Construction

## Nothing inside is special.

The arm is built only from finished Checkmate nodes and a hub. No springs, counterweights or one-off parts. Links, base and handle are the only Leader-specific hardware.

- A spare part is one node on a shelf
- A repair is a node swap, measured in minutes
- Each node ships with its own test card
- Kinematics matched to your follower arm

Price of an hour of finished teleop data, early 2024 to March 2026.

**06** Questions

**Who is Checkmate Dynamics?**

A robotics hardware company in Dallas, Texas. We design motion, sensing and sync hardware (SmartStepper, SmartServo G, Contour, the Sync Beacon and Hub 8 Pro) and build station products from it.

**What happens when something breaks?**

Every Leader joint is the same kind of node, so a repair is a swap, not a visit. Service plans include advance replacement; terms are confirmed before a plan starts.

**Do you see our data?**

No. Recordings stay on your machines and everything works on-prem. We see only the reports you choose to send us.

**Do the devices touch our network?**

No. The beacon and Contour are USB devices with no radio and no network connection. The recorder plugin runs on your PC.

**Will the beacon affect our training data?**

It should not: the beacon is a separate USB device and changes nothing on your cameras. We walk through the details on a call.

**We already sync our cameras in hardware.**

Keep it. Hardware sync ties those cameras together; the beacon checks every stream on the station, including webcams, joint logs and wrist depth, and certifies each episode.

**Can we try it first?**

Start with a Skew Audit on one station. Register your interest and we agree the details on a call.

**03** Upgrade path

## Board, then node, then geared node.

Start with a board on your own motor, add our motor and housing later, then a reducer. The node keeps its identity and calibration history as it grows.

**Fig. 02** SmartServo G stack Concept render

**04** Who it’s for

## For people who build.

01

### Printer and CNC upgraders

Closed-loop axes that report a stall instead of shifting a layer, on STEP/DIR from Klipper, Marlin or GRBL.

02

### Robot-arm builders

Joints that know their position, on one cable, without a pile of separate electronics.

03

### LeRobot and SO-101

Quiet, backdrivable joints with calibration that lives on the node, for leaders, wrists and grippers.

04

Field-oriented control on gimbal motors without assembling a driver, encoder, MCU and supply.

05

### Camera and astro rigs

Silent, repeatable moves for sliders, pan heads and turntables.

### University labs

Documented parts for courses and research rigs.

# Perfect the nodes. Build everything else from them.

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/company.html

Company | Dallas, Texas

Checkmate Dynamics designs complete motion, sensing and sync nodes, sells them to people building robots, and builds its own station products from the very same units.

**01** Principles

## How we build.

01

### One family

Same cable, connector, bus, clock, app and look across every product. Own one node and you know the next.

02

### Plug in, then work

Plug it in and it’s found, named and ready. Settings exist; nobody needs them to start.

03

### Measured, not promised

We publish measurements. Anything not yet measured is marked as a target, and every unit ships with its own test card.

04

### Value first

We aim for the best part in its class, judged by the work it saves you.

05

### Built from the same nodes

Our larger products are assemblies of the retail nodes, hub and cable. Improve one node and everything improves.

06

### Continuity

Identity, calibration and history travel with a node from a maker’s bench to a data floor.

07

### Your data is yours

Everything works on-prem; the cloud is optional. Station devices have no radio, any node radio is off until you turn it on in the app, and we never receive your recordings.

08

### Finished

Closed housings, labeled ports, and one look from the product to the box to this page.

**02** Record

## From one stepper board to a platform.

It started with SmartStepper, a closed-loop NEMA 17 that runs on a USB-C charger. Then SmartServo G for brushless gimbal motors, Contour for depth, cycloidal reducers for both node families, the Sync Beacon for station timing, and Hub 8 Pro to power and connect it all.

**Fig. 01** SmartStepper 17, exploded Concept render

# This site collects nothing about you.

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/privacy.html

Privacy | Updated October 14, 2026

No cookies, no analytics and no third-party requests. The forms are off, so nothing you type here is sent anywhere.

**01** Plainly

## What this site does

It shows pages, images and type that we host ourselves. Fonts are served from this site. It sets no cookies and uses no local storage for tracking. There are no analytics, advertising or social-media scripts.

## What the host sees

Any web host keeps ordinary server logs, such as your IP address, the page and the time. We do not use them to track people or build profiles.

## Links to other sites

Some figures link to their sources on other sites. Those sites have their own privacy practices.

## Email

You reach us by email. We use what you send only to reply to you, we do not sell it, and we delete it on request. If we add forms, this page will first say exactly what they collect and why.

## Contact

Questions about this page: [contact@checkmatedynamics.com](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Privacy%20question).
